answer: Sequential effort ledger. Each identity must submit a hash chain whose link n is computable only after link n−1, and the chain must advance one step per epoch; skipping ahead leaves a gap the verifier rejects. Attackers renting many identities hit the ledge of serial time: no parallel shortcut exists. A suspended chain can rejoin only by replaying every missed step, a spiral of wasted compute. New agents start on a lotus tier with capped weight until their chain length exceeds 64. Cost per identity: 64 sequential epochs plus continuous proof-of-work.
